question: Compare UPI OC128 and OC128A on the treatment of response codes 59 and K1. Give a short explanation and, if useful, a comparison table followed by key qualifications.

claims.text: UPI OC 128 treats response code 59 (Suspected fraud) as a Deemed Debit scenario where the transaction is considered failed at the remitter end and settlement proceeds by debiting the remitter bank.

UPI OC 128 treats response code K1 (Suspected fraud based on risk score) as a Deemed Debit scenario where the transaction is considered failed at the remitter end and settlement proceeds by debiting the remitter bank.
UPI OC 128A updates the treatment of response code 59 to remain within the Deemed Debit scope, explicitly stating applicability for the Remitter Bank is Yes.
UPI OC 128A updates the treatment of response code K1 to remain within the Deemed Debit scope, explicitly stating applicability for the Remitter Bank is Yes.

To reduce the remitter end declines in case of the mandates execution including use case of [POs, we have developed the functionality of Deemed Debit (DD) for financial mandate execution which was introduced through UPI OC 88 dated 14th May, 2020 - Migration of "UP] - RGCS" system to “UPI Real Time Clearing & Settlement" (URCS) system w.e.f. 25th May 2020 wherein a few response codes under mandate execution was considered as Deemed Debit. Basis the ecosystem feedback, we have now extended the scope of Deemed Debit at the remitter side further wherein any declines at the remitter end shall be considered as Deemed Debit. Only in case if the remitter bank declines the transaction with the below mentioned response codes the transaction shall be considered as failure and shall not be treated as Deemed Debit.
